title: Integral closure of quasi-coherent algebras commutes with smooth space pullback
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $g:Y\to X$ a smooth morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], meaning that every compatible pair of etale scheme charts $U\to Y$, $V\to X$ with a map $U\to V$ over $g$ gives a smooth scheme morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal B$ be a commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebra on the small etale site whose underlying module is quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Write $\operatorname{IC}_X(\mathcal B)\subseteq\mathcal B$ for the unique quasi-coherent subalgebra of [lem-sfb-space-quasicoherent-integral-closure], characterized on affine etale tests by elements satisfying monic polynomials over the base ring. Tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] of this inclusion identifies $g^*\operatorname{IC}_X(\mathcal B)$ with $\operatorname{IC}_Y(g^*\mathcal B)$ as subalgebras of $g^*\mathcal B$. The identification is the one induced by pulling back the inclusion, hence is compatible with isomorphisms of $\mathcal B$ and with identity and composite smooth pullbacks. No finite-type, reducedness, injectivity of the structure map, or Noetherian hypothesis on $\mathcal B$ or the spaces is imposed.

source.place: Tag 082E (lemma-integral-closure-smooth-pullback); compatibility is the equality as subalgebras in this lemma. Integral closure itself is the existing Tag 0820 node, not a new assertion here.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\operatorname{IC}_X(\mathcal B)$. The integral-closure node supplies its quasi-coherence and its inclusion in $\mathcal B$; pullback preserves quasi-coherence for both modules. Choose affine etale charts $V_i\to X$ covering $X$. Their base changes cover $Y$; choose affine etale scheme charts $U_{ij}$ covering $Y\times_X V_i$. Thus each $U=\operatorname{Spec}T$ maps to $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ over $g$, and these $U$ cover $Y$. By the chartwise smoothness hypothesis $R\to T$ is smooth. Write $B=\mathcal B(V)$ and $C=\mathcal C(V)=\operatorname{IC}_R(B)$. The normalized tensor-composition comparison identifies $(g^*\mathcal B)|_U$ with the pullback to $U$ of $\mathcal B|_V$, and does the same for $\mathcal C$ and its inclusion. The affine-chart calculus identifies these restricted quasi-coherent modules with their associated modules on the affine schemes. For the scheme map $h:U\to V$, the Zariski--etale comparison identifies the etale tensor pullback of the etale module associated with a quasi-coherent Zariski module $M$ on $V$ with the etale module associated with the Zariski pullback $h^*M$, naturally in $M$, and its sections on the open $U$ are those of $h^*M$. Applying affine pullback sections to $h^*$ of the Zariski modules of $B$ and $C$ gives $(g^*\mathcal B)(U)=T\otimes_R B$ and $(g^*\mathcal C)(U)=T\otimes_R C$. Naturality of that sections isomorphism identifies the pulled-back inclusion with $1_T\otimes(C\hookrightarrow B)$, sending $t\otimes c$ to $t\otimes c$. These identifications respect algebra multiplication because on local tensor sections multiplication is $(t\otimes b)(t^{\prime}\otimes b^{\prime})=tt^{\prime}\otimes bb^{\prime}$.

source.place: Tag 082E (lemma-integral-closure-smooth-pullback), affine reduction, expanded using Tags 0820, 03GA, 03LZ and 01I9.

proof.text: Apply smooth ring base change to $R\to T$ and $R\to B$. It says that $T\otimes_R C\to\operatorname{IC}_T(T\otimes_R B)$ is an isomorphism induced by the same tensor of the inclusion. Composing with the subalgebra inclusion into $T\otimes_R B$ is therefore injective and has image exactly that integral closure. The space integral-closure node applied to the quasi-coherent algebra $g^*\mathcal B$ identifies this target with $\operatorname{IC}_Y(g^*\mathcal B)(U)$. The restrictions to $U$ of the quasi-coherent modules $g^*\mathcal C$, $g^*\mathcal B$ and $\operatorname{IC}_Y(g^*\mathcal B)$ are the associated modules of their sections on $U$, so these statements about sections on $U$ hold for the restricted sheaf maps on the etale site of $U$. Consequently the pulled-back map is locally a monomorphism and has exactly the required subalgebra as image. The ring theorem imposes no condition on $R\to B$ beyond being a commutative algebra map.

source.place: Tag 082E (lemma-integral-closure-smooth-pullback), affine reduction, expanded using Tags 0820, 03GA, 03LZ and 01I9.

proof.text: These local maps all come from the single sheaf map $g^*(\mathcal C\hookrightarrow\mathcal B)$. On overlaps their factorizations through $\operatorname{IC}_Y(g^*\mathcal B)$ agree, since its inclusion in $g^*\mathcal B$ is injective on sections. The sheaf gluing axiom therefore gives a global comparison map. Its local inverses also agree: after the same injective inclusion they are inverses of the very same map. They glue to its inverse. This proves the asserted identification as subalgebras, including monicity of the pulled-back inclusion. The argument uses an etale cover, not an assertion that every affine chart of $Y$ maps into a single affine chart of $X$.

source.place: Tag 082E (lemma-integral-closure-smooth-pullback), affine reduction, expanded using Tags 0820, 03GA, 03LZ and 01I9.

proof.text: An algebra isomorphism carries an element satisfying a monic polynomial to one satisfying the image monic polynomial, and its inverse gives the converse. The resulting integral-closure maps commute with the inclusions. The comparison above is uniquely determined by its composite with the inclusion, so is natural in algebra isomorphisms. For the identity pullback the tensor unit sends $a\otimes c$ to $ac$, hence gives the identity on this subalgebra. For successive smooth pullbacks, the tensor-composition comparison sends $a\otimes(b\otimes c)$ to $a\,h^\sharp(b)\otimes c$. Both the successive and composite comparisons send this local tensor to that same element in the pulled-back ambient algebra. Local tensors generate the sheafified tensor product, so the maps agree; injectivity of the integral-closure inclusion gives the claimed equality into the subalgebra.
